source: MAFF Svay Rieng Provincial Department of Agriculture / Polinuovo (Robolino) Program - Report: "Project for Supporting and Promoting New Local Initiatives" - Subject: "Corn Cultivation Techniques via Farmer-Led New Initiative" (បច្ចេកទេសដំដុៈដំណំពោតសអមផ្តូចផ្តើមថ្មីរបស្កសិករ), Ruessei Am village, Khsem commune, Kampong Ro district, Svay Rieng province
text:
This report documents a farmer-led on-farm research trial for corn (ពោតស, maize) cultivation in Ruessei Am village, Khsem commune, Kampong Ro district, Svay Rieng province, conducted under the "Polinuovo" (also transliterated Robolino) local-initiative support program. The rationale given is that many farmers already practice agriculture but rely only on inherited, traditional techniques passed down from their ancestors, resulting in low yields that do not meet demand; some farmers have innovative ideas for new techniques but are reluctant to experiment themselves for fear of failure and loss of money and time. The program therefore provided funding and technical coordination (via provincial Department of Agriculture staff working with the program) to let willing, motivated farmers test their own techniques/ideas for growing corn, with results to be documented and shared with other farmers in the community afterward. Farmers were selected based on interest, willingness to participate, and having suitable land, labor and some of their own material resources.

Stated objectives of the trial: to carry out farmer-initiated experimental research on corn cultivation; to study and understand the crop's growth pattern; to track yield results; to monitor pests and diseases that damage the crop; and to find solutions to problems that arise unexpectedly during cultivation.

Responsible parties: the Svay Rieng Provincial Department of Agriculture and the Polinuovo program working team, consisting of two named staff — a deputy head of the provincial Department of Agriculture (who also served as provincial program coordinator) and an agricultural extension office official (who handled technical coordination, training and accounting).

Work activities included: liaising with local authorities; holding meetings with farmers to publicize the program and select willing volunteer farmers; visiting farmers' proposed trial sites; discussing the program's experimental objectives with farmers; agreeing on each farmer's own experimental topic/technique; explaining the experimental method and distributing record-keeping documents/plans for farmers to log their own trial design; monitoring the trials and collecting farmers' data; compiling data; producing an evaluation report; and finally reconvening with all participating farmers to present each individual's trial results.

The common land preparation and planting method recorded across the trial plots was: plow the soil twice to a depth of about 2.5 cm; leave the soil to dry/fallow for roughly 6-7 days before working it further; form raised planting beds (rows) about 1 meter wide; apply a base/bottom fertilizer dose of about 0.5 kg per plot before planting; and then apply three subsequent top-dressing (supplemental) fertilizer applications at later growth stages, each combining a chemical fertilizer (ជីគីមី) and a natural/organic fertilizer (ជីមជ្ញាទិ), with the amounts of each increasing at each of the three top-dressing rounds (roughly 5 kg chemical + 9 kg organic at round 1, 8 kg chemical + 18 kg organic at round 2, and 11-12 kg chemical + 20-21 kg organic at round 3, per plot, though exact figures varied slightly farmer to farmer). Planting dates recorded for individual farmers' plots were in late June to early July 2014 (e.g. 27 June 2014 for one farmer's plot, 3 July 2014 for several others). Growth was tracked weekly (stalk height in cm and leaf count) from week 1 through week 7 after planting, and harvest was carried out in three successive picking rounds starting roughly 80-85 days after planting.
